title: Ethics bills on nepotism, lobbyists and ex-employees
summary: On October 20, a committee took up Bill 100, which would set lobbyist rules, but no vote appears on the motions to replace it with a revised version or to recommend passage. The chair said lawyers would work on amendments during the recess. Attorneys disagreed on whether lobbying the Planning Commission would be covered, and the rules would start July 1, 2027.

boards.name: Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: Motion to replace Bill 100 (2026) with the proposed CD1 version attached to the chair's amendment summary form: The motion was made and seconded, but no vote appears in the recording.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: Motion to recommend passage of Bill 100 (2026) on first reading, including any non-substantive revisions: The motion was made and seconded, but no vote appears in the recording.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the lawyers would use the recess to work on amendments, which the committee would take up after returning.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The attorneys present did not all agree on whether lobbying before the Planning Commission would be covered.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: Members asked if people lobbying the Planning Commission would have to register, and one attorney disagreed with the others.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The director said she would get back to the committee on how the rules apply to boards and commissions.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The rules would take effect July 1, 2027, with the first report due January 31.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The director said lobbyists would file expenditure reports twice a year, compared with four times a year for the state.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The director said lobbyists would be able to register online.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: A deputy corporation counsel (a County lawyer) said a $5,000 penalty would be fine.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The director said the Board of Ethics prefers a penalty of up to $5,000, matching the state.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The director said a $5,000 penalty was replaced with a reference to fines that Bill 55 would cap at $1,000.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The chair will work with staff to bring back the two deferred bills, with no date set yet.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: Staff will send the Board of Ethics a written question on how often its lobbyist list is updated.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The committee deferred Bill 99, which would set rules against nepotism (giving jobs to family members).
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: A council member moved to state in the law that it applies retroactively, meaning to past actions too.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: Motion to amend Bill 55-2025 with the proposed CD1 version: A motion to replace Bill 55 with the proposed new (CD1) version was made and seconded; the captions do not clearly show its vote.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: A proposed new version would start the six-year clock when the violation happened instead.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: Bill 55 would let the Board of Ethics pursue violations for up to six years after a worker leaves county jobs.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The Board of Ethics chair said the board lost three recent cases because the employees had left county service.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: A testifier who served on the Board of Ethics spoke in favor of Bills 55, 99, and 100.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: A committee will hear the board's priorities on July 28, 2026, including its nepotism law and lobbyist rules.
timeline.body: Maui Board of Ethics

timeline.text: The report noted the county has no nepotism policy, which is a rule about hiring relatives.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The committee will take up good governance reform bills being worked on with the Board of Ethics after the fraud report meeting.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee
